source.title: projUNN: efficient method for training deep networks with unitary matrices
source.authors: B. Kiani; Randall Balestriero; Yann LeCun; S. Lloyd

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training results for unitary convolutional networks on MNIST and CIFAR-10, settings that extend the claim’s general subject. The reported CIFAR-10 results are test accuracy, while the MNIST depth experiment reports training accuracy.
record.gate_note: The study does not test any listed version’s defining comparison or mechanism. The MNIST depth experiment compares unconstrained CNNs with projUNN-T, not plain networks with and without identity shortcuts. CIFAR-10 ResNet accuracies are test accuracies, so they are not rows for training-error outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study uses norm-preserving unitary transformations to develop and benchmark a training method. Its results do not isolate initialization, identity shortcuts, batch normalization, width-dependent spurious minima, or learning-rate stability thresholds. The MNIST training results and CIFAR-10 test results do not test the specified versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the CNN experiments. The paper's principal conclusion is that low-rank projected updates can preserve competitive unitary-network performance with nearly optimal runtime scaling. Its preliminary CNN results suggest greater stability at depth on MNIST, while constrained CIFAR-10 models remain below standard models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses unitary/orthogonal-constrained networks and RMSprop; the claim versions describe other training recipes and comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: For CIFAR-10, performance differs between Resnet9 and Resnet18 and between standard and unitary/orthogonal convolution parameterizations. For the MNIST depth experiment, the authors report different training and test accuracy for the unconstrained CNN and projUNN-T at depth 100.

fits_no_version.finding: At depth 100 after 100 epochs on MNIST, unconstrained and projUNN-T CNNs achieve 92.7% and 95.7% training accuracy, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Maintaining unitary convolutional weights improves training accuracy in this tested deep MNIST CNN setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix G.4 reports poor performance with Haar or near-Haar initialization; the authors instead use identity or Henaff initialization, with task-specific preferences described in D.2 and D.3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization choice affects performance within constrained unitary recurrent networks, even among norm-preserving initializations.

record.problems: The depth comparison’s training accuracies are stated only for depth 100 at 100 epochs; no uncertainty is reported. The paper’s checklist says error bars were not reported. The MNIST accuracy result does not establish training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: CIFAR-10 Resnet9 and Resnet18 accuracy comparisons in Section 5 and Appendix D.5/Table 3 are test accuracy, not training accuracy or training error. The MNIST Figure 5 depth curves do not provide textual per-depth training-accuracy values; only the depth-100, 100-epoch caption values are included.

untested.parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error under the specified gradient-training recipes, including corrupted labels and capacity or stopping conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student spurious-minimum frequencies and the effects of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation across depths and its prevention by identity shortcuts; the special-initialization and Fixup cases.
Activation-matched initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth, orthogonal-versus-Gaussian initialization, and very deep plain convolutional training.
Loss and curvature trajectories relative to learning-rate stability thresholds, recovery, and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text does not expose readable Figure 5 curve values. Its depth comparison is described as test accuracy, so it cannot establish training-error degradation across depths. Appendix G.4 concerns initialization within constrained unitary models and does not isolate V4's proposed signal-preservation mechanism.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 training classification error, corrupted or random labels, smaller-model or early-stopping outcomes, or the stated SGD/Adam comparison.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment, spurious-minimum rate, or width comparison.

Does not compare plain batch-normalized CNNs with and without identity shortcuts. Its MNIST depth experiment compares unconstrained and unitary networks; it does not test the listed ImageNet/CIFAR-10 residual-shortcut claim or the cited special-initialization and Fixup cases.
Does not compare the listed activation-matched, orthogonal-versus-Gaussian, or 10,000-layer initialization conditions.
Does not study learning rates above a stability threshold, sharpness, curvature, or divergence.
Does not test batch normalization’s speed or learning-rate tolerance against the listed settings, or Fixup.

rows.subject: unconstrained CNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained CNN on MNIST for 100 epochs at depth 100; training accuracy reported.
rows.note: The caption gives training accuracy but does not provide a baseline value or describe the result as training classification error.
rows.check: The reported 92.7% training accuracy is valid and implies 7.3% training classification error; the record's assertion that accuracy cannot establish classification error is incorrect. However, this single-depth MNIST result does not measure any listed version. The 100-epoch result is separate from the caption's 50-epoch depth experiment.

rows.subject: projUNN-T
rows.operation_detail: Trained unitary CNN on MNIST for 100 epochs at depth 100; training accuracy reported.
rows.note: The caption gives training accuracy but does not provide a baseline value or describe the result as training classification error.
rows.check: The reported 95.7% training accuracy is valid and implies 4.3% training classification error. R1 supplies an unconstrained comparator, with accuracy 3 percentage points lower. Maintaining unitary constraints throughout training does not isolate an initialization effect or test identity shortcuts.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
